name: Brussels South Charleroi Airport
before:
Sold as a Brussels airport and 46 km from it, which is the first thing to make clear. Charleroi is 7 km from its own city centre and is Belgium's second busiest airport, with 10,504,554 passengers in 2024.

The transfer is well organised but it is a transfer. A shuttle bus runs continuously between the airport and Brussels-Midi station, roughly every thirty minutes and timed to the flights, with fares starting at 14.99 euros through Flibco. There is also a coach to Brussels-Central.

For the Belgian rail network, the Airport Express bus A runs to Charleroi-South station every thirty minutes, taking about twenty minutes, and from there SNCB trains reach Brussels, Namur, Liège and Mons. A combined bus and train ticket to any Belgian station can be bought in the terminal.

Shuttles also run to Luxembourg and Lille.

The airport is a busy general aviation field as well, with three flight schools based here, and flying at Gosselies goes back to 1919.
after:
Ryanair sells it as Brussels Charleroi, but it is about 45 km south of Brussels, which is the first thing to make clear to a client. It is Belgium's second busiest airport, 7 km from the centre of Charleroi, its own city. Eurostat counted about 11.2 million passengers there in 2025.

The transfer into Brussels is well organised, but it is a transfer. Flibco runs shuttles to Brussels-Midi station every 20 minutes, taking about 55 minutes, with fares from 14.99 euros. Shuttles also run to Luxembourg and Lille.

For the Belgian rail network, TEC buses run to Charleroi Central station in about 20 minutes, and the airport gives four departures an hour. A combined train and bus ticket is sold on the SNCB website.
